subject: chemistry
title: Entropy Expanse: Disorder and Direction
welcome_lead: Quantify disorder with ΔS and predict spontaneous change.
meta_desc: A-Level chemistry adventure on entropy and the second law of thermodynamics.
final_note: You have grasped the universal drive towards disorder.

concepts.def: Number of ways particles can be arranged.

walkthroughs.body_html:
ΔS > 0 when: gases form, mol number increases, solid dissolves, temperature rises.

Example: CaCO3(s) -> CaO(s) + CO2(g) has positive ΔS because a gas appears from a solid.

ΔS_surr = -ΔH / T. Units: convert ΔH from kJ to J before dividing by T in K.

Exothermic reactions warm surroundings, raising their entropy (ΔS_surr positive). At low T, |ΔS_surr| is larger.

A change is spontaneous when ΔS_total > 0. This is equivalent to ΔG < 0 at constant T and p.

Endothermic dissolving (NH4NO3 in H2O) is spontaneous because ΔS_system is highly positive enough to outweigh negative ΔS_surr.
